root_cause: The cluster's API server authorized IP ranges (203.0.113.10/32, 198.51.100.0/24 in az-aks-show.json) do not include the new agent pool's egress address — the NAT gateway public IP 192.0.2.55 (az-network-public-ip-show-natgw.json, applied by vmss-agents.json) — so API server connections from retail-deploy-agents are dropped at the control plane and kubectl i/o-times-out, while VPN laptops succeed because 203.0.113.10/32 is the VPN range.
evidence: az-network-public-ip-show-natgw.json: the agents' NAT gateway egress IP is 192.0.2.55, absent from the authorized ranges
pipeline-log.txt: kubectl from selfhosted-azdo-egress-0 i/o-times-out dialing the API server FQDN; the VPN-based laptop run succeeds
service-connection.json: the ARM service connection validates fine (red herring — auth is not reached)
fix: Add the agent pool's NAT gateway public IP 192.0.2.55/32 to the cluster's authorized IP ranges (az aks update --api-server-authorized-ip-ranges with the existing ranges plus 192.0.2.55/32, or its stable /24) so API server traffic from retail-deploy-agents is allowed.
